E1.evidence: Issue gives a full reproducer node and console log; the reporter states "After sending an `async_send_goal() `request, the result_callback is immediately invoked, and the returned result.code is UNKNOWN." Maintainer sea-bass confirms the diagnosis direction ("Yep, that's exactly it! If it works well, definitely put up a PR") and merged PR #3125 / backport #3127 (https://github.com/moveit/moveit2/issues/3117).

units_identified: move_group with pilz_industrial_motion_planner MoveGroupSequenceAction capability (action server /sequence_move_group)
E2.evidence: The reported composition is the reporter's client node calling action:/sequence_move_group on move_group. The defect is a multi-threading race among the server's own callbacks, caused by the server creating its action-server callback group as Reentrant; it is triggered by an ordinary sequential client and does not depend on any assumption the client makes about the server, so it would occur with any correct client. Reporter: "When I removed the `action_callback_group_ `parameter in the `create_server() `function, the program was able to run stably, indicating a potential multi-threading race condition." Maintainer: "If Pilz sequence planning is not thread-safe, I could see how that causes problems." The fix is confined to the server's callback-group type: "-      context_->moveit_cpp_->getNode()->create_callback_group(rclcpp::CallbackGroupType::Reentrant);\n+      context_->moveit_cpp_->getNode()->create_callback_group(rclcpp::CallbackGroupType::MutuallyExclusive);" (https://github.com/moveit/moveit2/pull/3125).

E3.evidence: PAIR: the client's goal/result requests feed the server's action interface ("sequence_move_group_client_ = rclcpp_action::create_client<moveit_msgs::action::MoveGroupSequence>(this, \"/sequence_move_group\");").

E4.evidence: Observed wrong result: "[INFO] [1732012243.106202476] [sequence_move_demo]: Planning request result code= 0" followed by "Planning request unknown result code"; "It stops after 5-10 runs" (https://github.com/moveit/moveit2/issues/3117).

notes: ROS 2 Humble, CycloneDDS, source build. Fix: moveit2 PR #3125 (main, merge 6d94dfb719f28215a0d9ba21eac1b0f8a6146f9b, head 9da70e4d2897e69f2b1df020d1aefc7af40e335d) and humble backport PR #3127 (merge ed38b2d1d94bbf8ee6f48c36ace96135a0a11656); fork commit e3cef36e15e86b65731a21f44698241b0bc164f6 is the same one-line change on the humble base. Classification caveat (confidence medium): the source does not settle where inside the server process the race lies. The maintainer reads it as Pilz sequence planning not being thread-safe, and the reporter found that mutexes on goal_handle_ and move_state_ only "improved stability"; the reporter also wrote "I suspect this might be related to `rclcpp_action`". In the attached move_group log the failing goal is logged as "[1732012243.106392151] [move_group.rclcpp_action]: Accepted goal f978765172cc299a7059b8ec689ea" while the client logged its UNKNOWN result at 1732012243.106202476, and the server went on to "goal_handle->succeed(action_res);" for that goal. If one instead takes the composition to be the Pilz capability plugin and the rclcpp_action library (plugin choosing a Reentrant callback group for an rclcpp_action server), the case could be read as a CONCURRENT library-API interaction; no source statement documents that rclcpp_action assumption, so it is not specified here.
